question: The Golden Quadrilateral is a project of Government of India which is related to______
solution:
The correct answer is __**Highways**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Golden Quadrilateral project is one of the largest highway projects in India and was initiated by the Government of India.
 
• It connects four major metropolitan cities: Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata, forming a quadrilateral.
 
• The project was launched in 2001 by then Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee under the National Highways Development Project (NHDP).
 
• The total length of the Golden Quadrilateral is approximately 5,846 kilometers.
 
• The primary aim of this project is to improve road connectivity and boost economic development by facilitating the faster movement of goods and passengers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Highways Development Project (NHDP)**

 
 
• The NHDP is a project to upgrade, rehabilitate, and widen major highways in India to international standards.
 
• It was implemented by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).
 
• The NHDP is divided into several phases, with the Golden Quadrilateral being part of Phase I.
 
 
 
• **Bharatmala Pariyojana**
 
 
• Bharatmala Pariyojana is an umbrella program for the highways sector that focuses on optimizing the efficiency of freight and passenger movement across the country.
 
• It aims to develop 65,000 km of national and economic corridors, border and international connectivity roads, coastal and port connectivity roads, and greenfield expressways.
 
 
 
• **Expressways in India**
 
 
• Expressways are high-speed roads with controlled access and are designed to handle high volumes of traffic.
 
• The Delhi-Mumbai Expressway is one of the largest ongoing expressway projects in India.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Economy**
 
 
• Improved road infrastructure reduces transportation costs and travel time, thereby enhancing trade and commerce.
 
• Better connectivity promotes regional development and attracts investments in various sectors.
